answer: A staking bond makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock collateral before it can trade, like a mesa that only stands if its base is solid. An opal registry then ties every bond to one verified hardware attestation, so one operator cannot mint a thousand cheap copies. Peers check the bond on a public terrace of reputation scores before dealing, and slashing burns the stake of any identity caught cheating, so the cost of a Sybil swarm exceeds any profit it could steal.
